Hi Daniel — really glad the demo was useful. Attaching a short SOW template and a pricing matrix to get the conversation moving (see attachments). High-level answers up front:

- Pricing: see attached spreadsheet (tabbed by term). We publish a baseline per-GPU-month rate; effective customer rate depends on commit size + term.
- Discounts: typical model: 10% on 24-month, 15% on 36-month for baseline commits; incremental volume tiers (+20% sustained volume) get additional step discounts. We can be flexible on cases where usage is very predictable.
- Billing vs activation: Standard is invoice from the contract start date. For enterprise deals we can offer an activation-based invoicing start (billing begins when the pool is green) if you include a 30–60 day activation window in the contract.
- Throughput SLA: We guarantee a per-request p99 latency target and a committed throughput (rps / GPU-equivalent) for the pool. If we miss SLA we offer service credits; if capacity constraints persist we provide automatic fallback to compatible model variants and burst capacity while we remediate. Exact credit formula is in the SOW.
- Lead time: Typical lead time is 4–6 weeks to provision and validate a dedicated pool (depends on region). If you sign by Feb 1 we can target activation the week of Mar 15.

Next steps: I'll loop in Karthik from pricing so we can present a firm quote and a couple of ramp schedules (soft start vs immediate activation).

Best,

Proposed draft pricing:
- 12-month: baseline 1.00 GPU-eq/mo price (no term discount).
- 24-month: baseline * 0.90 (10% term discount).
- 36-month: baseline * 0.82 (18% term discount for multi-year + early-commit incentive).

Can we commit to the 18% for 36-month? Also need to confirm SLA credits for throughput misses and whether we can promise burst-to-shared for the first 30 days to smooth early spikes (no extra charge).

— Sofia

Hi Daniel — Karthik here, pricing lead. Appreciate the clear questions; below are firm answers we can include in the SOW and the commercial term sheet. I've included a short example calculation and a proposed fallback/remediation commitment.

1) Volume ladder / "sustained" definition:
- "Sustained usage" is defined as the 30-day trailing average of GPU-equivalent utilization, measured as average concurrent streams normalized to our GPU-equivalent model. We'll include the exact telemetry SNIPPET in the SOW so both sides can independently verify.

2) Mobilization deposit and invoicing:
- We can apply the 30% mobilization deposit as a credit against the first two monthly invoices (50% of deposit applied to invoice 1, 50% to invoice 2) instead of forfeiture.
- Activation-based billing: we will not invoice until pool-green if the contract explicitly states a 45-day activation window. If activation completes earlier we'll invoice from the actual pool-green date.

3) SLA credit example (throughput miss):
- Scenario: committed throughput = 10,000 rps across the pool. Observed throughput drops to 7,000 rps for 6 contiguous hours during business hours.
- Credit calculation: we calculate the percentage shortfall (30% shortfall) * hours impacted / total monthly hours * monthly committed fee = preliminary credit. For the scenario above this equates to ~ (0.30 * 6 / 720) * monthly_fee => ~0.25% of the monthly fee credited.
- If multiple or sustained misses occur, credits scale up and we will propose a remediation plan (priority hardware replacement, temporary burst to shared pool, and a dedicated escalation engineer). Credits are the primary contractual remedy; for repeat SLA failures we can negotiate additional make-good (one-off manual credits or short-term rate relief).

4) Hardware delays and protections:
- If activation is delayed beyond the agreed 45-day activation window due to supply or provisioning issues on our side, options are:
  a) extend activation window at no additional charge and apply a daily credit for the number of days beyond 45 up to a capped percentage of fee, or
  b) if delay exceeds 60 days, either party may exit without penalty and the mobilization deposit will be fully refunded to you.

Proposed commercial offer (summary):
- 12-month: list price (no term discount).
- 24-month: 10% term discount on list.
- 36-month: 18% term discount + early-commit signing credit of 2% applied to first year invoice if signed by Feb 1.
- Volume ladder: >150 GPU-eq sustained => additional 8% discount on incremental capacity.
- Activation: 45-day window; mobilization deposit 30% applied as credit to first two invoices.
- SLA: Credits as described; burst to shared pool for up to 30 days at no extra charge during initial activation period.

I'll draft a short commercial term sheet and a DocuSign packet. If that looks good, Sofia can send the final to legal.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call to walk legal through the SLA math.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Pricing | Redwood Inference
